us16_systems.topic: Health coverage, financing and cost: Israel's National Health Insurance Law and four funds vs the US mixed system

claims.text: Israel's National Health Insurance Law was passed by the Knesset in 1994 and took effect on 1 January 1995; membership in one of the four funds became compulsory with guaranteed acceptance; before it, about 95% were insured and Clalit required Histadrut membership or dependency on a member

The NHI law ended the link between fund eligibility and party or union membership, ended patient selection ('cream skimming'), defined a government-funded basket and earmarked a health tax; capitation by age, sex, area and a few severe diseases
Fund shares 2024: Clalit 50.96%, Maccabi 27.48%, Meuhedet 13.99%, Leumit 7.57%

Commonwealth Fund (2026): health tax 3.2% of income up to 60% of average wage and 5.2% above; government 65% of health spending in 2024; total spending NIS 146bn (USD 39.4bn) in 2024, 7.3% of GDP, USD 3,941 per capita; out-of-pocket 19.9% of spending in 2024

Commonwealth Fund: basket updated annually on the Public Committee's recommendation; 117 medicines and technologies recommended Feb 2025; specialist copay NIS 22–35 first visit per quarter; drugs 10% (generic) / 15% (brand) of maximum price, min NIS 18; 88% of adults had supplementary plus commercial cover in 2022
Commonwealth Fund: asylum seekers, undocumented migrants, foreign workers and B1 visa holders are excluded from NHI; soldiers and prisoners (about 2%, 2021) covered by separate systems
Commonwealth Fund: average wait for endocrinologist or neurologist 50 days in Q1 2024; 495 general acute beds per 100,000 in 2023

Angel et al. (2021): non-public sources 36% of national health expenditure; Brookdale 2016: ~85% of households held fund supplementary insurance, 57% commercial; national spending 6.9% to 7.4% of GDP since the law
Census 2025: 26.7m (7.9%) uninsured all year, not statistically different from 2024; employment-based 53.5%, public 35.8%, Medicaid 17.1% (down 0.5 pt), Medicare 20.1%

2024 uninsured 8.0% (27.1m); enhanced ACA premium tax credits expired end of 2025; KFF: average premiums paid by subsidized marketplace enrollees rose from $888 to $1,904 a year (114%); marketplace enrollment fell from ~24.2m to ~23m
Census via KFF Health News: more than 50m (nearly 17%) uninsured in 2009; about 42m in 2013; 29m (9.1%) in 2015; 28.1m (8.8%) in 2016, a record low
CBO via KFF: 2025 reconciliation law (signed 4 July 2025) increases uninsured by about 10m by 2034 (7.5m Medicaid, 2.1m Marketplace); with enhanced credit expiry, 14.2m

KFF EHBS 2025: average family premium $26,993, single $9,325; workers pay $6,850 for family cover; family premiums +6% in 2025 vs wages +4% and inflation 2.7%; single deductible $1,886; 34% have deductible >= $2,000
CMS NHE 2024: $5.3tn, $15,474 per person, 18.0% of GDP, +7.2%
Peterson-KFF: per capita spending $353 in 1970 ($2,208 in 2024 dollars); share of GDP peaked at 19.7% in 2020; out-of-pocket $1,632 per person in 2024; prescription drugs 8.8% of spending in 2024
WHO/World Bank out-of-pocket share of current health spending: US 15.1% (2000), 12.4% (2010), 10.9% (2023); Israel 29.5% (2000), 23.8% (2010), 20.5% (2023)

Peterson-KFF (SIPP, Dec 2021): Americans owed at least $220bn in medical debt; ~20m adults owe >$250, ~14m >$1,000, ~3m >$10,000; 13% of Black adults, 8% of White, 3% of Asian report medical debt; 11% of all-year uninsured vs 8% of all-year insured

Dobkin, Finkelstein et al. (NEJM 2018): hospitalizations account for about 4% of bankruptcies among non-elderly adults, against a commonly cited ~60%; Himmelstein, Woolhandler and Warren replied that the method undercounts medical bankruptcy; the dispute is unresolved

Commonwealth Fund: Israel's Ministry of Health negotiates drug prices; maximum prices set from the three lowest of seven reference countries; 2024 maximum prices of 1,500 prescription drugs cut 3.6%; pharmaceuticals 12.9% of health spending in 2022, USD 405 per capita

Commonwealth Fund: mental health practitioners 104 per 100,000 (2021) vs OECD 123; psychiatric beds 36 per 100,000 (2024); post-7 October reforms funded by a health tax increase, hiring public therapists and multidisciplinary clinics; Rehabilitation Law (2000)

us16_outcomes.topic: Health outcomes over time, drug prices and mental health in Israel and the US

claims.text: CDC: US life expectancy 79.0 in 2024 (78.4 in 2023); men 76.5, women 81.4; infant mortality 552.5 per 100,000 births in 2024 vs 560.2 in 2023 (not significant); suicide 10th leading cause, 48,824 deaths, 13.7 per 100,000 age-adjusted; unintentional injury rate fell 14.4%
CDC 2023 provisional: US IMR 5.61; Black non-Hispanic 10.93, White non-Hispanic 4.48, Hispanic 5.03, AIAN 9.20, Asian 3.44

Taub (2010): in 1980 life expectancy of Israeli Jews, the US and other OECD countries was about 74; Israeli Arabs over two years lower; since then rose over seven years for Israeli Jews and Arabs vs about four in the US; Israeli Arab infant mortality reached US rates by mid-2000s

Israel Health Ministry inequality report (2022 data): national life expectancy 82.7; highest for Jews/non-Arabs 84.3 (Tel Aviv), highest for Arabs 80.1 (north); infant mortality Arabs 5.1 vs Jews 2.1 per 1,000; doctors and beds unevenly distributed; north and south 81.3

RAND (2022 data): US drug prices 278% of prices in 33 other high-income countries; brand-name 422% gross, over three times after estimated rebates; unbranded generics lower in the US than in most comparison countries

KFF: under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 the first 10 negotiated Medicare prices took effect 1 Jan 2026 (CMS: $6bn, 22% net savings had they applied in 2023); 15 more from 1 Jan 2027 (44%, incl. Ozempic/Wegovy); 15 Part B/D drugs selected Jan 2026 for 2028; 2025 reconciliation law widened orphan-drug exclusion, CBO cost $8.8bn

Bank of Israel: 2015 reform moved mental health insurance to the health funds (July 2015), NIS 2bn added 2015–16, then only a one-off NIS 100m to 2024; State Comptroller (2018 data) average ~150-day wait for psychotherapy

Bank of Israel: after 7 Oct 2023 CBS share reporting depression rose from 23–25% to 34% in 2024; treatment 14% (Jan 2024) to 18% (Oct 2024); public wait ~6.5 months in Mar–Apr 2024; 42% of treatment-seekers went private vs 38% health funds; National Mental Health Program Jan 2024 NIS 1.4bn a year; 2025 health tax increase ~NIS 1bn a year; psychiatrists ~0.17 per 1,000 vs OECD ~0.21 (2023); therapists scarce in periphery and Arab community
SAMHSA NSDUH 2024: 52.1% of adults with any mental illness received mental health treatment in the past year; not comparable with 2022–23 due to questionnaire change
